[[File:Ronaldo vs. FC Schalke 04 (16854146922).jpg|thumb|upright|[[Cristiano Ronaldo]] is [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]'s all-time leading goalscorer with 450 goals in 438 games in total.|alt=A man in a white shirt and shorts looking upwards.]]

[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]] is a Spanish professional [[association football]] club based in [[Madrid]]. The club was formed in 1902 as ''Madrid Football Club'', and played its first competitive match on [[1902 Copa de la Coronación#Semifinals|13 May 1902]], in the [[1902 Copa de la Coronación|Copa de la Coronación]] semi-final.<ref name="Real Madrid turns 106 (I)">{{cite web | title = Pre-history and first official title (1900–1910) | url = http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202730681095/noticia/Noticia/Real_Madrid_turns_106_(I).htm | publisher = Realmadrid.com | access-date = 12 July 2008 | author = Luís Miguel González | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20081229094130/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202730681095/noticia/Noticia/Real_Madrid_turns_106_%28I%29.htm | archive-date = 29 December 2008 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> Real Madrid currently plays in the Spanish top-tier [[La Liga]], having become one of the founding members of that league in [[1929 La Liga|1929]], and is one of three clubs, the others being [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[Athletic Bilbao]], to have [[List of unrelegated association football clubs|never been relegated]] from the league. They have also been involved in European football ever since they became the first Spanish club to enter the European Cup in [[1955–56 European Cup|1955]], except for the [[1977–78 Real Madrid CF season|1977–78]] and [[1996–97 Real Madrid CF season|1996–97]] seasons.

This list encompasses the major honours won by Real Madrid and records set by the club, their managers and their players. The player records section includes details of the club's leading goalscorers and those who have made most appearances in first team competitions. It also records notable achievements by Real Madrid players on the international stage, and the highest transfer fees paid and received by the club.

The club currently holds the record for the most [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup / UEFA Champions League]] triumphs, with 15, and the most La Liga titles, with 36. Additionally, Real has won the [[Copa del Rey]] 20 times, the [[Supercopa de España]] 13 times, the [[Copa de la Liga]] once, the [[Copa Eva Duarte]] once, the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] twice, the [[UEFA Super Cup|European/UEFA Super Cup]] six times, the [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|Intercontinental Cup]] three times, the [[FIFA Intercontinental Cup]] one time, the [[FIFA Club World Cup]] five times, the [[Latin Cup]] twice and [[Copa Iberoamericana]] once. Powered by its fifteen European Cups, Real Madrid have a distinction of being the most successful club in terms of international titles, having amassed 35 pieces of silverware, more than any other team in the world. On the domestic front, its 71 titles rank second to Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/about-real-madrid/honours/football |title=Trophies |publisher=[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] |access-date=8 April 2010}}</ref> The club's record appearance maker is [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]], who made 741 appearances from 1994 to 2010; the club's record goalscorer is Portuguese forward [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], who scored 450 goals in 438 appearances through all competitions from 2009 to 2018.

==== Consecutive scoring ====
[[File:Arthur Johnson 1902.jpg|thumb|upright|[[Arthur Johnson (footballer, born 1879)|Arthur Johnson]], the first player to score an official goal in Real Madrid's history.]]
*Most consecutive matches with goals: '''12'''&nbsp;– {{flagicon|POR}} [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], 25 August 2014 – 1 November 2014 and 10 February 2018 – 18 April 2018<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/real-madrid/20180419/442725285898/cristiano-ronaldo-iguala-la-mejor-racha-goleadora-de-su-carrera.html |title=Cristiano Ronaldo iguala la mejor racha goleadora de su carrera |date=19 April 2018 |publisher=Mundo Deportivo |access-date=7 September 2024}}</ref>
*Most consecutive matches with goals in [[La Liga]]: '''11'''&nbsp;– {{flagicon|POR}} [[Cristiano Ronaldo]],  25 August 2014 – 22 November 2014<ref>{{cite web|url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/kylian-mbappes-scoring-run-4740|website=[[IFFHS]]|title=Mbappé's scoring run for Madrid concedes only to CR7's|access-date=12 November 2025|date=11 November 2025}}</ref>{{refn|group=note|On 7 May 2014, Cristiano Ronaldo played against [[Real Valladolid]] for only eight minutes before leaving due to injury without scoring a goal. This eight-minute appearance disrupted a streak between 2 March and 22 November 2014, spanning 19 matches. He had scored in eight consecutive matches before the game and in 11 consecutive matches after it. If he scored in this match, he would have scored in 20 consecutive matches.}}
*Most consecutive matches with goals in [[Copa del Rey]]: '''7'''
** {{flagicon|ESP|1874}} [[Gaspar Rubio]], 16 December 1928 – 27 January 1929
** {{flagicon|HUN}}{{flagicon|ESP|1945}} [[Ferenc Puskás]], 19 June 1960 – 1 June 1961
*Most consecutive matches with goals in [[UEFA Champions League]]: '''11'''&nbsp;– {{flagicon|POR}} [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], 3 June 2017 – 11 April 2018<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tudn.com/futbol/uefa-champions-league/cristiano-el-pulverizador-de-records-primer-jugador-en-marcar-en-11-partidos-seguidos-de-champions |title=Cristiano, el pulverizador de récords: primer jugador en marcar en 11 partidos seguidos de Champions |date=11 April 2018 |publisher=TUDN |access-date=7 September 2024}}</ref> <span style="color:green"><sup>(Record)</sup></span>

==== Fastest goals ====
*Fastest goal: '''13 seconds'''&nbsp;– {{flagicon|CHI}} [[Iván Zamorano]] v [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], [[1994–95 La Liga]], 3 September 1994<ref name="Zamorano">{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/deporte/futbol/2012/goles-rapidos/ |title=Los goles más rápidos de la liga |publisher=MARCA.com |access-date=25 September 2013}}</ref>
*Fastest goal in [[Copa del Rey]]: '''15 seconds'''&nbsp;– {{flagicon|ESP|1945}} [[Paco Gento]] v [[Racing de Santander|Racing Santander]], [[1960–61 Copa del Rey]], 28 May 1961<ref name="Paco Gento">{{cite web |title=Biblioteca Nacional de España – La Vanguardia (29 May 1961), p.13 |url=https://prensahistorica.mcu.es/es/catalogo_imagenes/grupo.do?path=352349&posicion=13&presentacion=pagina&registrardownload=0 |website=Prensa Histórica |publisher=Ministerio de Cultura y Deporte |language=es |access-date=16 August 2025}}</ref>
*Fastest goal in international competitions: '''34 seconds'''&nbsp;– {{flagicon|TUR}} [[Arda Güler]] v [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]], [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League]], 15 April 2026<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/02a4-2065d3ad61f5-d3ad2c2b1ca9-1000--bayern-munchen-4-3-real-madrid-agg-6-4-late-goals-send-baye/ |title=Bayern München 4-3 Real Madrid (agg: 6-4): Late goals send Bayern to semi-finals in Champions League classic |publisher=UEFA |date=15 April 2026 }}</ref>{{refn|group=note|Arda’s goal is considered earlier by fractions of a second than [[Felo (footballer, born 1936)|Felo]]’s goal against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in 1962.<ref name="Felo">{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/real-madrid/2016/11/02/581a5279e5fdea52148b46a4.html |title=Este es el gol más rápido del Madrid en Europa... ¡a los 35 segundos! |date=2 November 2016 |publisher=MARCA.com |access-date=5 January 2024}}</ref>}}
*Fastest goal in final match: '''1 minute'''&nbsp;– {{flagicon|ESP|1945}} [[Enrique Mateos]] v [[Stade de Reims|Stade Reims]], [[1959 European Cup final]], 3 June 1959
*Fastest goal by a substitute: '''14 seconds'''&nbsp;– {{flagicon|BRA}} [[Vinícius Júnior]] v [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]], [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League]], 21 October 2020<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2020/10/21/champions/1603305425_796478.html |title=Vinicius, de récord: marcó a los 14 segundos de pisar el campo |date=21 October 2020 |publisher=as.com |access-date=29 October 2025 |language=es}}</ref>
*Fastest goal by a substitute in [[La Liga]]: '''31 seconds'''&nbsp;– {{flagicon|ESP}} [[Marco Asensio]] v [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], [[2019–20 La Liga]], 18 June 2020
*Fastest goal by a debutant: '''62 seconds'''&nbsp;– {{flagicon|BRA}} [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]] v [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]], [[2002–03 La Liga]], 6 October 2002

==== Latest goals ====
*Latest goal: '''121:40 minutes'''&nbsp;– {{flagicon|MAR}} [[Brahim Diaz]] v [[Atlético Madrid]], [[2024 Supercopa de España]], 10 January 2024
*Latest goal in regulation time: '''99:34 minutes'''&nbsp;– {{flagicon|FRA}} [[Kylian Mbappé]] v [[Rayo Vallecano]], [[2025–26 La Liga]], 1 February 2026
*Latest goal being the opener: '''107 minutes'''&nbsp;– {{flagicon|ESP|1945}} [[Pau Vidal (footballer, born 1920)|Pau Vidal]] v [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], [[1947 Copa del Generalísimo final]], 22 June 1947
*Latest goal in regulation time being the opener: '''96:55 minutes'''&nbsp;– {{flagicon|POR}} [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] v [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League]], 11 April 2018
*Latest goal under exceptional circumstances: '''95 days'''&nbsp;– {{flagicon|MEX}} [[Hugo Sánchez]] v [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]], [[1988–89 La Liga]], 3 May 1989{{refn|group=note|In [[La Liga]] against Osasuna, the match began on 28 January 1989, and continued until the 43th minute when the fans throwing fireworks at [[Paco Buyo]] caused the game's suspension with the score at 1–0 for Osasuna. Later, on 3 May 1989, after 95 days, the second half was played at [[La Romareda]], and [[Hugo Sánchez]] managed to score the equalizer in the 86th minute, marking the longest goal from the opening whistle in Real Madrid's history.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2016/09/09/57d29ffb22601db24e8b45af.html|title=10 moments which define the Real-Osasuna rivalry|website=MARCA}}</ref>}}

==== By position ====
*Most goals scored by a goalkeeper: '''0'''{{refn|group=note|No goalkeeper has ever scored for Real Madrid in an official match throughout the club's history. The closest moment for a goalkeeper to score was [[Thibaut Courtois]] against [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] in [[2019–20 La Liga]] on 15 December 2019, when he headed the ball in the final minutes of the match, forcing a difficult save from the goalkeeper, and [[Karim Benzema]] followed up to score.}}
*Most goals scored by a defender: '''128''' – {{flagicon|ESP}} [[Fernando Hierro]], 1989–2003{{refn|group=note|Fernando Hierro played as a midfielder for three seasons between 1991–92 and 1993–94, after [[Radomir Antić]] converted him from centre-back to midfield. [[Benito Floro]] continued to deploy him in that role over the following two seasons, before [[Jorge Valdano]] restored him to the centre-back position in 1994–95.<ref>{{cite web |title=Nyom as a forward and position changes that amazed football: Hierro, Loren, Luis Enrique, Molina… |url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/primera-division/2025/10/02/nyom-delantero-cambios-posicion-asombraron-futbol-hierro-loren-luis-enrique-molina.html |website=MARCA |author=José Luis Hurtado |date=2 October 2025 |access-date=5 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Apuntes de la Historia – Recordando a Fernando Hierro |url=https://madridistareal.com/apuntesdelahistoria-recordando-a-fernando-hierro/ |website=MadridistaReal |date=29 June 2018 |access-date=5 February 2026}}</ref> During those three seasons in midfield, he scored 56 goals, while he netted 72 goals as an out-and-out defender across his remaining seasons at Real Madrid. Excluding this period in midfield, [[Sergio Ramos]] is the highest-scoring defender in Real Madrid history, with 101 goals.}}
*Most goals scored by a midfielder: '''171''' – {{flagicon|ESP}} [[Pirri]], 1964–1980

** {{flagicon|ESP|1937}} [[Jacinto Quincoces]] v [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], [[1940–41 La Liga]], 1 December 1940{{refn|group=note|On 1 December 1940, during a match between Real Madrid and Barcelona at [[Camp de Les Corts]], Spanish defender [[Jacinto Quincoces]] was forced to take over as goalkeeper in the 77th minute after the team's regular keeper, [[Enrique Esquiva]], suffered a back injury following a collision with both Quincoces and Barcelona forward Julián Vergara. With no substitutions allowed at the time, Quincoces stepped into goal for the remainder of the match. Despite being a central defender, he made two notable saves, preventing further goals. The match ended in a 3–0 victory for Barcelona.<ref>"Barcelona, 3 – Madrid, 0." ''La Vanguardia Española'', 2 December 1940, p. 3. [https://prensahistorica.mcu.es/es/catalogo_imagenes/grupo.do?path=458580&presentacion=pagina&posicion=3&registrardownload=0 Historical Press Archive of Spain]. Retrieved 5 August 2025.</ref>}}
** {{flagicon|ESP|1945}} [[Sabino Barinaga]] v [[Atlético Madrid|Atlético Aviación]], [[1945–46 La Liga]], 16 December 1945{{refn|group=note|[[José Bañón]] suffered a knee injury caused by [[José Juncosa]], Atlético’s forward, which caused him to lose consciousness, prompting Barinaga to guard Real Madrid’s goal for the remaining seven minutes of the first half. After the break, Bañón returned to his position that day.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Jornada: diario de la tarde: Año IX Número 2337 – 16/03/1949
 |url=https://prensahistorica.mcu.es/es/catalogo_imagenes/grupo.do?path=569818&presentacion=pagina&posicion=4&registrardownload=0

 |accessdate=13 August 2025
}}</ref>}}
** {{flagicon|ESP|1945}} [[Macala (footballer)|Macala]] v [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]], [[1948–49 La Liga]], 6 March 1949{{refn|group=note|name=RMvsCelta1949|On 6 March 1949, during the match between Real Madrid and Celta Vigo at the Balaídos stadium, [[José Bañón]], Real Madrid’s goalkeeper, sustained a hand injury two minutes before the end of the first half after a collision with Celta Vigo players' feet. He was temporarily replaced by [[Macala (footballer)|Macala]] for the remaining two minutes of the half. During halftime, it was confirmed that the goalkeeper had suffered a dislocated hand. Although the backup goalkeeper, [[Adauto Iglesias]], was part of the squad traveling to Vigo, he was unable to participate due to illness. Consequently, coach [[Michael Keeping]] decided to deploy [[Sabino Barinaga]] as goalkeeper, field José Bañón as a winger, and return Macala to his natural position. This lineup remained unchanged until the end of the match.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Jornada: diario de la tarde: Año IX Número 2308 – 07/03/1949
 |url=https://prensahistorica.mcu.es/es/catalogo_imagenes/grupo.do?path=737978&presentacion=pagina&posicion=4&registrardownload=0
 |website=Biblioteca Virtual de Prensa Histórica – Ministerio de Cultura y Deporte
 |accessdate=13 August 2025
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
 |title=La Prensa: diario de la tarde de información mundial: Año IX Número 2419 – 07/03/1949
 |url=https://prensahistorica.mcu.es/es/catalogo_imagenes/grupo.do?path=96052&presentacion=pagina&posicion=4&registrardownload=0

}}</ref>}}
** {{flagicon|ESP|1945}} [[Sabino Barinaga]] v [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]], [[1948–49 La Liga]], 6 March 1949{{refn|group=note|name=RMvsCelta1949}}{{refn|group=note|Barinaga is the only outfield player in Real Madrid’s history who has taken the goalkeeper position more than once. * Oldest-living former Real Madrid player: '''{{Age in years and days|1931|12|19}}''' – {{flagicon|ESP}} [[José Vicente (footballer)|José Vicente]], born on 19 December 1931{{refn|group=note|José Vicente is the oldest former player whose survival has been verified. Other players, such as Manuel Rocha and Pelayo Camino, have neither been confirmed to be alive nor documented as deceased, as no reliable information about their current status is available.}}
* Earliest-appearing living Real Madrid player: '''{{Age in years and days|1954|9|12}}''' – {{flagicon|ESP|1945}} [[Mario Duran Rubíes|Mario Duran]] v [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], [[1954–55 La Liga]], 12 September 1954

=== Internationals ===
*First international appearance by a Real Madrid player: [[Juan Monjardín]], {{fb-rt|ESP|1874}} v {{fb-rt|POR}}, 17 December 1922

*First international appearance by a Real Madrid non-Spanish player: [[Raymond Kopa]], {{fb-rt|FRA}} v {{fb-rt|PAR}}, 8 June 1958
*First international appearance by a non-Spanish player to have played for Real Madrid: [[Fernando Giudicelli]], {{fb-rt|BRA}} v {{fb-rt|YUG}}, 14 July 1930 (he later joined Real Madrid in 1935)
*Most international caps as a Real Madrid player: '''176''' – [[Sergio Ramos]], {{fb-rt|ESP}}
*Most [[cap (sport)|capped]] player to play for Real Madrid: '''234''' – [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], {{fb-rt|POR}} (89 caps whilst at Real Madrid)
*Most international goals as a Real Madrid player: '''63''' – [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], {{fb-rt|POR}}
*[[List of men's footballers with 50 or more international goals|Most international goals]] by a player who played for Real Madrid: '''146''' – [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], {{fb-rt|POR}} (63 goals whilst at Real Madrid)

On 17 March 2026, the CAF Appeal Board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match for temporarily refusing to play and leaving the pitch in protest of a refereeing decision.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/ce949glzzglo |title=Morocco awarded Afcon title after CAF overturns result |work=[[BBC Sport]] |date=17 March 2026 |access-date=17 March 2026}}</ref> Pursuant to articles 82 and 84 of the competition regulations, the final was awarded as a 3–0 win for Morocco, thereby retroactively declaring them as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions and stripping Senegal of the title.<ref name="CAF appeal">{{cite web |url=https://www.cafonline.com/news/caf-appeal-board-media-statement/ |title=CAF Appeal Board Media Statement |publisher=[[Confederation of African Football]] |date=17 March 2026 |access-date=17 March 2026|archive-date=17 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260317220033/http://web.archive.org/screenshot/https://www.cafonline.com/news/caf-appeal-board-media-statement/ |url-status=live }}</ref>}}

==== Matches time ====
* Shortest match: '''6 minutes''', against [[Real Sociedad]], [[2004–05 La Liga]], 5 January 2005{{refn|group=note|The match began on 12 December 2004, and continued until the 88th minute when a false [[bomb threat]] forced the referee to suspend the game with the score at 1–1. Later, after 24 days, the remaining six minutes, including four minutes of added time, were resumed on 5 January 2005. [[Zinedine Zidane]] scored a penalty just four minutes into the restart.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bomb threat at Bernabeu stadium |date=12 December 2004 |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/4090669.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |accessdate=2025-12-10}}</ref>}}
* Longest match: '''149 minutes''', against [[Real Betis]], [[1965–66 Copa del Rey]], 15 May 1966{{refn|group=note|The minutes were distributed as follows: ninety minutes of regular time, thirty minutes of the first extra period, two additional periods of ten minutes each, and nine minutes of the fourth extra period, which ended with Real Betis’ decisive goal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://prensahistorica.mcu.es/es/catalogo_imagenes/grupo.do?path=1000256375&posicion=13&presentacion=pagina |website=Biblioteca Virtual de Prensa Histórica |access-date=2025-12-10}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bdfutbol.com/en/p/p.php?id=503853 |title=Player profile at BDFutbol |website=BDFutbol |access-date=2025-12-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://as.com/futbol/2006/01/18/mas_futbol/1137569212_850215.html |title=Multifútbol – AS.com |website=AS.com |date=18 January 2006 |language=es |access-date=22 February 2026}}</ref>}}

=== Clean sheets ===
*Most clean sheets in a season: '''30 matches''' – [[2010–11 Real Madrid CF season|2010–11 season]] 
*Most clean sheets in a season in [[La Liga]]: '''21 matches''' – [[2023–24 Real Madrid CF season|2023–24]]
*Most clean sheets in a season in [[Copa del Rey]]: '''8 matches''' – [[2013–14 Real Madrid CF season|2013–14]] <span style="color:green"><sup>(Spanish record)</sup></span>
*Most clean sheets in a season in [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup / UEFA Champions League]]: '''10 matches''' – [[2015–16 Real Madrid CF season|2015–16]] <span style="color:green"><sup>(Shared record)</sup></span>
*Most consecutive clean sheets: '''8 matches''', 6 January 2014 – 28 January 2014
*Most consecutive clean sheets in [[La Liga]]: '''7 matches'''
** 11 December 1994 – 5 February 1995
** 7 September 1997 – 27 October 1997
*Longest run without a clean sheet: '''24 matches''', 26 January 1941 – 18 January 1942
*Longest run without a clean sheet in [[La Liga]]: '''26 matches''', 8 May 1999 – 17 January 2000

=== Points ===
*Most points in a season:
**Two points for a win: '''66''' in 44 matches (in [[1986–87 La Liga|1986–87]] season) <span style="color:green"><sup>(Spanish record)</sup></span>
**Three points for a win: '''100''' in 38 matches (in [[2011–12 La Liga|2011–12]] season)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hispanicallyspeakingnews.com/latino-daily-news/details/fc-barcelona-ties-real-madrids-record-of-100-points/24879/ |title=Real Madrid record of 100 points a season |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151003202053/http://www.hispanicallyspeakingnews.com/latino-daily-news/details/fc-barcelona-ties-real-madrids-record-of-100-points/24879/ |archive-date=3 October 2015 }}</ref> <span style="color:green"><sup>(Shared record)</sup></span>
*Fewest points in a season:
**Two points for a win: '''17''' in 18 matches (in [[1929–30 La Liga|1929–30]] season)
**Three points for a win: '''62''' in 38 matches (in [[1999–2000 La Liga|1999–2000]] season)

== Other achievements ==
* Most appearances in the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup / UEFA Champions League]]: '''57''' seasons<ref name=UEFA1 /><!-- Until 2026–27 season-->
* First club to own the [[European Champion Clubs' Cup]]'s official trophy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c511b10d395-72f38b4cbce0-1000--how-uefa-honours-multiple-european-cup-winners/|title=How UEFA honours multiple European Cup winners|work=uefa.com|date=21 May 2018}}</ref>
* [[Forbes list of the most valuable sports teams#Number one by year|World's most valuable sports team]]: '''2013, 2014, 2015'''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/kurtbadenhausen/2013/07/15/real-madrid-tops-the-worlds-most-valuable-sports-teams/?sh=2b1498bb5f40|title=Real Madrid Tops The World's Most Valuable Sports Teams|work=Forbes|date=15 July 2020}}</ref>
* First club to win consecutive [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cups]] (1985 and 1986).
* Only team in UEFA club football history to defend both the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] and [[UEFA Champions League]] successfully.<ref name=NYT>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/05/26/sports/champions-league-real-madrid-liverpool.html|title=Real Madrid Beats Liverpool in Champions League Final on a Wonder and Two Blunders|publisher=NewYorkTimes|date=26 May 2018}}</ref>
* Only team to win consecutive [[FIFA Club World Cup#Performances by club|FIFA Club World Cup]] titles as well as three titles in a row (2016, 2017, 2018).
* First and only club to win three consecutive (or more) [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup / UEFA Champions League]] titles twice (1956–1960 and 2016–2018).<ref name=UEFA2 />
*First club to win consecutive [[UEFA Champions League]] titles and the only club to win three consecutive titles (2016, 2017, 2018).<ref name=UEFA2 />
* Most [[List of world champion football clubs#By club|club world championships]] titles: '''9'''
* [[Forbes list of the most valuable football clubs#Number one by year|World's most valuable football club]]: '''2013–2016, 2019–2020, 2022–2025'''
* [[Deloitte Football Money League#Summary table: Number of times appearing in Top 10 and Top 20|Highest-earning football club in the world]]: '''2006–2016, 2019, 2024–2025'''
* Most [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup / UEFA Champions League]] titles: '''15'''<ref name=NYT />
* Most [[UEFA Super Cup]] titles: '''6'''
* Most [[List of UEFA club competition winners#By club|UEFA club competition]] titles: '''26'''
* First club to defend the [[Double (association football)#European double|European Double]] successfully.
* Only club to win [[Three-peat#International|five consecutive]] [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup / UEFA Champions League]] titles (1956–1960).
* Most [[European Cup and UEFA Champions League records and statistics#All-time top 25 European Champion Clubs' Cup and Champions League rankings|European Cup / UEFA Champions League]] final appearances: '''18'''
* Most [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup / UEFA Champions League]] semi-final appearances: '''33'''
* Most consecutive seasons in the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]]: '''15''' (1955–56 to 1969–70)
* Most consecutive appearances in the [[UEFA Champions League]] group stage / league phase: '''30''' (1997–98 to 2026–27)<ref name=UEFA2>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/025a-0ea50ec92fd0-788683cd18ca-1000--competition-facts/|title=Competition facts|publisher=UEFA|date=1 January 2020}}</ref>
* Most consecutive seasons in the [[UEFA Champions League]] knockout phase: '''29''' (1997–98 to 2025–26)
* Most consecutive [[UEFA Champions League]] semi-final appearances: '''8''' (2010–11 to 2017–18)
* Most consecutive [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] final appearances: '''5''' (1956–1960)
* Most consecutive [[UEFA Champions League]] final appearances: '''3''' (2016–2018) (joint record)
* Most successful [[UEFA]] team to defend the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup / UEFA Champions League]] trophy: '''6'''/15
* Most times to win all [[UEFA Champions League]] group stage matches: '''3''' (2011–12, 2014–15 and 2023–24) (joint record)
* Most consecutive knockout tie wins in [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]]: '''20''' (1955–1960)
* Most consecutive knockout tie wins in [[UEFA Champions League]]: '''12''' (2016–2018)
